items.question: What does vibration analysis training cover?
items.answer: Course topics include vibration measurement, sensors, data collection, signal processing, time- and frequency-domain analysis, fault identification and balancing. The exact topics depend on the course.

items.question: Which analyst categories are covered?
items.answer: The supplied course information includes Category I exam preparation, Machinery Vibration Fundamentals Level II with partial preparation for Category II, and Intermediate Machinery Vibration Analysis Level III with partial preparation for Category III.

items.question: Is hands-on training available?
items.answer: The Advanced Vibration Analysis Training course is listed as five days and hands-on. The Dynamic Balancing of Rotors course includes demonstrations and hands-on exercises.

items.question: Is an online course available?
items.answer: The course information includes a two-day online course. Contact Vibrosine to enquire about training details.

items.question: What does vibration consultancy include?
items.answer: The consultancy service can include a plant visit, vibration data collection, machinery analysis, a report of findings and recommendations for corrective tasks.

items.question: What is included in the annual maintenance service?
items.answer: The AMC description covers selected troublesome machines and a monthly machine-performance report, including equipment-stop and line-stop KPIs.

items.question: Who leads the training?
items.answer: Training is led by Mr. Srinivasa Raghavan Balaji, Certified Vibration Analyst Category IV.

items.question: How can I contact Vibrosine?
items.answer: Call +91 98416 78380 or email vibrosine@gmail.com to ask about training or consultancy.
